messages:
alex: Noticed an uptick in 'unexpected-token' parse errors after we switched to chunk-envelopes. A few low-power clients (embedded/linux) are failing.
priya: Which clients? any major customers?
rene: Mostly older python sidecars and a bespoke C client used by a partner. They still stream-parse by newline. The envelope adds JSON and breaks their simple parser.
alex: Revert would be bad. We need those per-chunk metadata fields for scoring and observability. Short-term shim seems inevitable.
priya: Options: 1) ingress egress adaptor that strips envelope for detected legacy peers, 2) runtime toggles to emit legacy shape when header `x-rw-compat=legacy` present, 3) protocol-level backwards-bridge (dual emit).
rene: Dual emit = bandwidth tax, avoid. Runtime opt-in helps modern clients but doesn't rescue un-upgradable devices. So I favor an edge adaptor behind a feature flag.
alex: Key constraints: - keep cache keys stable (compute on canonical payload) - preserve stream ordering & timing - must not drop security-related meta fields.
priya: Detection heuristic: peek first 256 bytes. If it starts with '{"envelope"' and UA in legacy list OR UA missing, enable unwrap mode. Emit metric `compat.unwrapped_v1`.
rene: Implement with a small state machine: buffer until full JSON chunk -> extract payload -> write native frame. Timeout 200ms for partial frames, then abort with metric.
alex: Rollout: dev/stage smoke -> canary 2% -> 25% -> 100% in selected regions. Rollback triggers: parse error rate grows, p95 latency delta > 5ms.
priya: I'll draft the infra-runbook notes and make sure the adaptor adds header `x-rw-compat-injected: true` for debugging. Also add a graylist of fields allowed to be stripped.
rene: I'll own the adaptor PR. Alex pls coordinate customer outreach for the top 20 client_ua buckets.
infra-bot: deploy: feature/compat-unpack deployed to staging at 2024-08-10T08:22:01Z
alex: Thanks team. We'll revisit after 48h of staging metrics.
